last_material_result: One bounded distribution-led discovery round tested four stable local/everyday utility clusters: public-parking fee/discount decisions, bulky-waste disposal cost/free-pickup routing, nursing-room/baby-facility finding, and public locker finding. All four were rejected before promotion. Parking is already served by dedicated fee calculators and location/price maps; bulky-waste search is served by multiple nationwide fee databases, including products that already combine municipal fees with free appliance pickup and private-quote comparison; nursing-room discovery has multiple fresh public-data-backed maps/directories with amenity filters; public lockers already have a nationwide map with live vacancy support. These are not merely generic substitutes: incumbents already implement the obvious action layer, so a new zero-cost static entrant would need either proprietary freshness or a materially different decision wedge. No such wedge survived this round without adding maintenance or platform dependence.
economics: KRW0 spent. All tested clusters have plausible ad/affiliate traffic models, but incumbent feature depth makes expected organic acquisition too weak for a near-zero-maintenance clone. Avoid build cost and SEO maintenance until a sharper recombination is found.
next_checkpoint: Fresh DISCOVER next run using a different genetic mode, preferably cross-domain transfer or workflow-fragment. Bias toward stable local questions where existing results are directories/guides but do not yet compute or recommend the user's next action.
recommendation: DO NOT BUILD any candidate from this round. Continue discovery; require a decision/action wedge that incumbents do not already provide rather than another local directory or fee lookup.
